title: The VLA/ALMA Nascent Disk and Multiplicity (VANDAM) Survey of Orion Protostars. II. A Statistical Characterization of Class 0 and Class I Protostellar Disks
question: What are the dust disk radii and masses of Class 0, Class I and Flat Spectrum protostars in Orion, and how do they evolve and compare with Class II disks, regions and simulations?

data.arrays: Three scheduling blocks each executed three times (nine executions)

what.value: Protostar Lbol, Tbol, classes and SEDs

evidence.quote: We selected all Class 0, Class I, and Flat Spectrum protostars from the survey that had reliable measurements of bolometric temperature
We adopt $\kappa_{0.87mm}$ = 1.84 cm$^2$ g$^{-1}$ from (cite: ossenkopf1994)

what.value: Class II and other protostellar disk mass/radius samples for comparison

evidence.loc: 4.2 Protostellar Dust Disk Masses versus Class II Dust Disk Masses
evidence.quote: the Lupus disks are from (cite: ansdell2016), the Chamaeleon disks are from (cite: pascucci2016), the Upper Sco disks are from (cite: barenfeld2016) and the Taurus disks are from (cite: tripathi2017)

external_data.citation: ansdell2016; pascucci2016; barenfeld2016; tripathi2017; tychoniec2018; williams2019; sheehan2017b

recipe.method: Phase-only self-calibration then clean imaging with Briggs robust 0.5, uv>25 kλ
key_parameters: self-cal only when peak S/N>10; applymode=calonly

recipe.goal: Measure flux, size of each source
recipe.method: Elliptical Gaussian fits; disk radius = 2σ deconvolved major axis (FWHM×2.0/2.355 × distance)
key_parameters: sources with unreliable sizes (fixed to beam) excluded from radius analysis
assumptions: Gaussian 2σ approximates disk radius (~95% of flux)

recipe.method: Optically thin isothermal M=D²Fν/(κνBν(Tdust)) with Tdust=43 K (L/Lsun)^0.25
assumptions: T0 = 43 K for 1 Lsun at 50 au, from RADMC-3D models

recipe.method: Kaplan-Meier survival analysis with left-censoring, log-rank and Anderson-Darling tests, Gaussian CDF fit for mean
key_parameters: uncertainties from fitting the 1σ upper/lower bounds of survival CDF

recipe.method: Q≈2(M*/Md)(H/R) with fiducial M*=0.25 Msun, gas-to-dust 100

answer_key.quantity: Mean dust disk radius, Class I (all)
Mean dust disk radius, Flat Spectrum (all)
Mean dust disk mass, Class I (all)
Mean dust disk mass, Flat Spectrum (all)
Mean dust disk mass, Class 0 non-multiples

evidence.loc: 3.3 Distribution of Protostellar Dust Disk Masses

evidence.quote: We detected continuum emission associated with the protostars in 286 fields with at least S/N $>$ 3, corresponding to a 87% detection rate.

evidence.loc: 3.2 Continuum Emission at 0.87 mm and 9 mm
evidence.quote: fit with a constant spectral index ($\alpha$) of 2.24$\pm$0.03 using *scipy*

answer_key.quantity: Fraction of disks with R>50 au

evidence.loc: 4.3 Protostellar Disk Radii and Their Evolution
evidence.quote: the frequency of protostellar disks with radii greater than $\sim$50 au is $\sim$36% (153/(379+42))

evidence.loc: 3.3 Distribution of Protostellar Dust Disk Masses
evidence.quote: we find median dust disk masses of 25.7, 15.6, and 13.8 M$_{\ensuremath{\oplus}}$, respectively

evidence.loc: 3.5 Distribution of Protostellar Dust Disk Masses versus Radius and Inclinations
evidence.quote: The median and mean values of cos($i$) are 0.596 and 0.601, respectively

Which source flux/size entries were taken as upper limits and detection criteria for fitting imfit regions

missing_for_reproduction: Line-free channels and spectral window flagging
score_reason: Public data, clear recipe and tables of per-source values; some imaging parameters unstated.
rediscovery_reason: Public ALMA data, defined Gaussian-fit and mass recipe, numeric results; but heavy data volume and some missing settings.
